answer:
MAIN ANALYSIS COMPLETE — RESULTS AND DRAFTED HYPOTHESIS

Executed script: analysis_gardening_habitat.py (outputs saved to outputs/per_habitat_summary.csv, outputs/binomial_glm_marginal_means.csv, outputs/chi_square.csv).

===========================
A. DESCRIPTIVE RESULTS (632 plots, 10 habitats; primary: prop_gard = Σn.gard/Σn.total among non-native records)
===========================
Habitat | plots | invaded plots | n.gard | n.total | prop_gard (Wilson 95% CI) | mean n.gard/plot
Broad-leaved forests*  | 68  |  3 |  4 |   4 | 1.000 (0.51–1.00) | 0.059
Coniferous forests*    | 77  |  5 |  7 |   8 | 0.875 (0.53–0.98) | 0.091
Wetlands               | 38  | 21 | 29 |  52 | 0.558 (0.42–0.68) | 0.763
Coastal                | 29  | 16 | 23 |  43 | 0.535 (0.39–0.68) | 0.793
Scrublands*            | 106 |  3 |  2 |   5 | 0.400 (0.12–0.77) | 0.019
Riparian               | 61  | 32 | 35 |  96 | 0.365 (0.28–0.46) | 0.574
Meadows                | 39  |  5 |  4 |  13 | 0.308 (0.13–0.58) | 0.103
Urban                  | 65  | 54 | 45 | 151 | 0.298 (0.23–0.38) | 0.692
Croplands              | 92  | 51 | 20 | 108 | 0.185 (0.12–0.27) | 0.217
Rock outcrops*         | 57  |  1 |  0 |   1 | 0.000 (0.00–0.79) | 0.000
(* low-confidence: total invaded records < 10)

Absolute frequency (mean n.gard per plot) ranks differently: Coastal 0.79 ≥ Wetlands 0.76 > Urban 0.69 > Riparian 0.57 >> Croplands 0.22 > Meadows/forests/Scrublands/Rock outcrops (0.00–0.10). So gardening aliens are most frequent on the ground in Coastal, Wetland and Urban plots, while their RELATIVE share among invaders is highest in forests (low absolute richness, small n).

===========================
B. INFERENCE
===========================
1. Chi-square (10×2 gardening vs other, invaded records): chi2 = 48.83, df = 9, p = 1.8e-07 → pathway composition differs strongly across habitats. (Caveat: min expected cell 0.35 due to tiny counts in forest/rock habitats.)
2. Binomial GLM on the 191 invaded plots, cbind(n.gard, n.total−n.gard) ~ habitat (reference = Urban; deviance 218.0 on 181 df): habitat effect significant. Contrasts vs Urban: Wetlands +1.09 logit (p = 0.0010), Coastal +1.00 (p = 0.0048), Coniferous forests +2.80 (p = 0.0097), Croplands −0.62 (p = 0.0405); Riparian, Meadows, Scrublands n.s.; Broad-leaved forests and Rock outcrops show complete separation (their proportion is 1.00 and 0.00), so their coefficients/SEs are uninformative — flagged low-confidence.
3. Poisson GLM over all 632 plots, n.gard ~ habitat (Pearson dispersion 1.14 → Poisson adequate; LR vs intercept-only = 196.1, df = 9, p = 2.2e-37). Marginal means reproduce observed means (see table above). Rate ratios vs Urban: Croplands RR = 0.31 (p < 0.001), Broad-leaved forests RR = 0.085 (p < 0.001), Coniferous forests RR = 0.13 (p < 0.001), Meadows RR = 0.15 (p = 0.0003), Scrublands RR = 0.027 (p < 0.001); Coastal RR = 1.15 (p = 0.60), Wetlands RR = 1.10 (p = 0.68), Riparian RR = 0.83 (p = 0.40) — i.e., gardening-alien frequency per plot in Coastal/Wetlands/Riparian is statistically indistinguishable from Urban, while forests, meadows, scrublands, rock outcrops and croplands host far fewer. Rock outcrops estimate is degenerate (separation; all-zero counts).

===========================
C. SENSITIVITY & ROBUSTNESS
===========================
• Poisson/NB GLM with covariates (elevation, annual temperature, annual rainfall, urban.2009 & cropland.2009 at 1000 m, distance.road, distance.stream): habitat block LR = 75.6, df = 9, p = 1.2e-12 → the habitat effect persists after environmental adjustment. Covariates: elevation −0.0036 per m (p = 0.013), distance.stream + (p = 0.017); urban/cropland cover, temperature, rainfall, distance.road n.s. With covariates, gardening frequency remains significantly higher in Urban (RR 8.1, p = 0.0004), Riparian (RR 6.9, p = 0.0008), Wetlands (RR 6.7, p = 0.0017), Coastal (RR 5.3, p = 0.0083) vs Broad-leaved forests reference.
• Binomial GLM + covariates (invaded plots): Wetlands (p = 0.0051), Coastal (p = 0.0110) higher and Croplands (p = 0.0030) lower gardening share than Urban — the relative-share pattern also persists.
• Landscape-change flags (progressive/regressive 1956–2009): habitat effect unchanged (LR p = 1.3e-12).
• Spatial check (crude): residual vs nearest-neighbour residual r = 0.20, p = 4e-07 → mild positive spatial autocorrelation exists; p-values are anticonservative, but the effect sizes (LR 196 → 76 with covariates) far exceed what this would erase.

===========================
D. CONTEXT (framing only)
===========================
• Temporal table (Catalonia, regional species counts): gardening's share of introductions rose from 17% (pre-1500) to 45% (1501–1900), 49% (1901–1984) and 75% (1985–2019); chi2 = 230.4, df = 6, p = 6e-47. Gardening is now the dominant introduction route region-wide.
• invasion_success_pathways.csv (deduplicated to 77 species): 39/77 (50.6%) are gardening-introduced.

===========================
E. DRAFTED HYPOTHESIS (deliverable)
===========================
"The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies strongly and systematically with habitat type in the Barcelona province. Gardening-introduced aliens are most prevalent — both in absolute per-plot frequency (0.79 and 0.76 gardening species per plot in Coastal and Wetland plots, statistically indistinguishable from Urban at 0.69) and in their share of the non-native flora (≈54–56% of all non-native records in Coastal and Wetland habitats, rising to 87–100% in coniferous and broad-leaved forest plots, albeit on very few records) — while Croplands (19% gardening share; 0.22 per plot), Meadows, Scrublands and Rock outcrops are dominated by unintentionally introduced species and host very few gardening aliens. This habitat effect is robust: it remains highly significant after adjusting for elevation, climate, urban/cropland cover, and distances to roads and streams (habitat-block LR p ≈ 1e-12), and mirrors the regional temporal trend in which gardening has become the dominant introduction pathway (17% of introductions before 1500 vs 75% in 1985–2019). In short, human-ornamental (gardening) introductions concentrate in wet, coastal and urban habitats and in forest patches — wherever ornamental plantings and garden-escape propagule pressure meet moist or disturbed conditions — whereas agricultural and ruderal habitats are filtered more by accidental (seed-contaminant) introductions. Forest and rock-outcrop estimates are low-confidence due to very few invaded records, and plot-level p-values should be read with mild caution given detectable spatial autocorrelation."

===========================
F. LIMITATIONS
===========================
1. Small counts in Broad-leaved forests (n=4 records), Coniferous forests (n=8), Scrublands (n=5), Rock outcrops (n=1) → wide CIs, complete separation in GLMs; these habitat estimates are low-confidence.
2. Mild spatial autocorrelation (r = 0.20 between neighbouring-plot residuals) means stated p-values are somewhat optimistic.
3. No sampling-effort/detectability metadata; per-plot frequencies could partly reflect survey differences.
4. Correlational, not causal: habitat type is partially confounded with urban/cropland cover.
5. The regional temporal table cannot be cross-classified by habitat; it is context only. The species-level file cannot be joined to plots.

payload.hypothesis: The prevalence of non-native plants introduced via gardening varies strongly with habitat type in the Barcelona province: gardening aliens are most prevalent in absolute per-plot frequency in Coastal (0.79/plot), Wetland (0.76/plot) and Urban (0.69/plot) plots — statistically indistinguishable from one another — and constitute the majority share of the non-native flora in Wetlands (56%) and Coastal habitats (54%), rising to 87–100% in forest plots (low-confidence, few records). In contrast, Croplands (19% gardening share, 0.22/plot), Meadows, Scrublands and Rock outcrops are dominated by unintentionally introduced species and host few gardening aliens. This habitat effect persists after adjustment for elevation, climate, urban/cropland cover and distances (habitat-block LR p≈1e-12), and is consistent with the regional trend of gardening becoming the dominant introduction pathway (17% of introductions before 1500 vs 75% in 1985–2019).
payload.workflow: Read tab-separated invaded_niche_pathways.csv (632 plots); verified count identity and zero missing values; computed per-habitat prop_gard = sum(n.gard)/sum(n.total) with Wilson 95% CIs and mean n.gard/plot; chi-square test on 10x2 gardening-vs-other table; binomial GLM cbind(n.gard, n.total-n.gard) ~ habitat on 191 invaded plots with marginal means and contrasts (Urban reference); Poisson GLM n.gard ~ habitat on all 632 plots (dispersion 1.14) with rate ratios; covariate-adjusted sensitivity models (elevation, annual temperature/rainfall, urban/cropland 2009 at 1000 m, distances to road/stream) plus landscape-change robustness and a crude spatial autocorrelation check; temporal contingency table (chi-square across periods) and deduplicated species-level pathway shares used as framing context.
